page.title: Hybrid Event Production Explained
page.description: Learn the core workstreams, staffing, platform choices and timelines for producing a hybrid event, plus a checklist and cost models.
page.definition: Hybrid event production is the coordinated delivery of a live experience that combines an in‑person venue audience with a simultaneous online broadcast, covering run‑of‑show design, speaker rehearsal, backup streaming, audience engagement tools, registration integration, real‑time Q&A moderation, branded graphics and a replay turnaround within one to two days.
page.quick_answer: Lock the venue AV and streaming platform six to eight weeks out, then assign a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator for the live day.

sections.h2: What workstreams make up a hybrid event?

blocks.p: A hybrid event is built on eight workstreams, each owned by a single person and producing a concrete output.

sections.h2: Which roles are needed on show day?

blocks.p: Show day requires a show caller, speaker manager, moderator, platform operator, producer, camera operator, audio engineer and backup stream engineer.

ul: Show caller – owns the run of show and cues
Speaker manager – coordinates speakers and cues
Moderator – fields live Q&A and chat
Platform operator – drives the streaming software
Producer – oversees overall flow and contingencies
Camera operator – captures venue video feeds
Audio engineer – mixes venue and remote audio
Backup stream engineer – monitors redundant encoder

sections.h2: How do the three cost models differ?

blocks.p: Platform pricing falls into three models: per‑host licences sized by attendee capacity, self‑serve monthly plans, and annual contracts quoted by sales.

sections.h2: What is the typical timeline from brief to live?

blocks.p: A hybrid conference needs six to eight weeks of management, while a webinar can move in three to four weeks.

ol: Week one to two: intake, brief, platform lock
Week three to four: production design, speaker contracts
Week five to six: technical rehearsal, run‑of‑show finalisation
Week seven to eight: live show, post‑event delivery

sections.h2: How do you mitigate single points of failure?

blocks.p: Redundancy is built into streaming, power, staffing and communication paths.

ul: Backup encoder and secondary internet link

blocks.p: West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations.

faq.q: What is the difference between platform and production?
faq.a: The platform is the software that hosts the stream and registration; production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream that turn the platform into a live show. Both are purchased separately and must be coordinated from the start.

faq.q: How much does a moderated webinar typically cost?
faq.a: Published ranges show moderated webinars between two thousand five hundred and seven thousand five hundred dollars per production, depending on scope and crew size. This figure covers producer, moderator, backup stream and edited recording delivery. Travel and venue costs are not included.

faq.q: When should the full rehearsal happen?
faq.a: Run one full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before the event, followed by a technical check sixty minutes before going live. The rehearsal validates run‑of‑show timing, speaker cues, backup stream switch and audience engagement tools smoothly.

faq.q: What deliverables should I expect after the event?
faq.a: You receive a run of show, speaker brief and rehearsal notes, branded slide template and lower thirds, live producer log, Q&A moderation log, backup stream recording, edited full recording and short clips for distribution. All files are delivered within one to two days after the live session.
